name: Attack
description:
Attack Time
Sets the attack time of an ADSR envelope triggered by MIDI gate events and used to short initial steam signal; logarithmic control.

name: Decay
description:
Decay Time
Sets the decay time of an ADSR envelope triggered by MIDI gate events and used to short initial steam signal; logarithmic control.

name: Sustain
description:
Sustain Level
Sets the sustain level of an ADSR envelope triggered by MIDI gate events and used to short initial steam signal.

name: Release
description:
Release Time
Sets the release time of an ADSR envelope triggered by MIDI gate events and used to short initial steam signal; logarithmic control.

name: Velocity Amount
description:
Velocity Amount
Sets the amount to which the incoming MIDI velocity information is passed on to the ADSR envelope.

name: Envelope Key Scaling
description:
Keyboard Scaling Amount
Controls the amount of scaling applied to the envelope times by the incoming MIDI pitch information.. Turn to the left for no keyboard scaling, to the right for shorter envelope times on high notes.

name: DC / Noise
description:
Impulse Source
Crossfades between the DC component at the left and the filtered noise, controlled in this section, at the right. The mixed signal is used as steam input of the resonating pipe.

name: Noise Cutoff
description:
Noise Cutoff
Sets the cutoff frequency of the noise signal.

name: Noise Key Track
description:
Cutoff Key Tracking
Controls the amount of key tracking applied to the filter's cutoff frequency. Turn to the right for higher cutoff frequencies at high MIDI pitches.

name: Noise Velocity Track
description:
Cutoff Velocity Tracking
Controls the amount of velocity tracking applied to the filter's cutoff frequency. Turn to the right for higher cutoff frequencies at high MIDI velocities.

name: Noise Resonance
description:
Noise Filter Resonance
Sets the resonance of the filter applied to the noise signal. It is only active if <1-pole> is off.

name: Noise One Pole
description:
Filter Damping Amount
If on, a 1-pole filter is used with 12 dB damping / octave. If off, a 2-pole filter with 24 dB / octave is applied.

name: Tune
description:
Pipe Tuning
Adjusts the tuning correction of the pipe. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used for large scale corrections.

name: Fine
description:
Pipe Fine Tuning
Adjusts the tuning correction of the pipe. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used for fine corrections.

name: Sample Correction
description:
Sampling Rate Error Correction
Adjusts the tuning correction of the pipe. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used to compensate Reaktor's sampling rate influence on the tuning.

name: Tune MW
description:
Modulation Wheel Tracking
Sets the amount of pitch modification by the MIDI modulation wheel. This simulates pitch changes of pipes that get blown softer or harder.
Refer also to the <MW Filter> section.

name: Polarity
description:
Polarity
Switches the polarity of the pipe, simulating different modes of real pipes. Technically speaking, this value determines wether a phase inversion will be applied to the reverberating signal within the pipe. Refer also to the <Push-Pull> section.

name: Allpass Tune
description:
Pipe Tuning
Adjusts the tuning correction of the additional allpass filter / delay. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
If the allpass filter / delay is switched off in the <Allpass> section, this control shows no effect.
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used for large scale corrections.

name: Allpass Fine
description:
Pipe Tuning
Adjusts the tuning correction of the additional allpass filter / delay. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
If the allpass filter / delay is switched off in the <Allpass> section, this control shows no effect.
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used for fine corrections.

name: Allpass Sample Correction
description:
Sampling Rate Error Correction
Adjusts the tuning correction of the pipe. This correction becomes necessary as there are certain problems in the implementation of the physical modell of the pipe which is mainly based on a delay / feedback unit. Its delay time adjusts the pitch of the sound; however, additional signal modification processes within this unit and Reaktor's sampling rate interfere with this delay time, resulting in detuning of the sound. 
If the allpass filter / delay is switched off in the <Allpass> section, this control shows no effect.
Use the <A440> section to produce a reference signal for tuning; this knob can be used to compensate Reaktor's sampling rate influence on the tuning.

name: Allpass MW
description:
Modulation Wheel Tracking
Sets the amount of pitch modification by the MIDI modulation wheel. This simulates pitch changes of pipes that get blown softer or harder.
If the allpass filter / delay is switched off in the <Allpass> section, this control shows no effect.
Refer also to the <MW Filter> section.

name: Diffusion
description:
Diffusion Amount
Sets the amount of diffusion within the additional delay unit. Technically speaking, with a value of 0 this unit becomes an allpass filter. Turn it to the left for additional attack effects of the pipe's sound. It also enhances the sound of harmonic frequencies which are not multiples of the main pitch, like e. g. in bells.

name: Allpass On
description:
Allpass Filter / Delay Switch
Turns the additional delay unit on or off. As it contains a diffusion control, it is very similar to an allpass filter. Its delay time can be adjusted in the <Allpass Tune> section. Switch on for additional attack effetcs of the pipe's sound.

name: Offset
description:
DC Offset
Sets the offset which is added to the reverberating steam signal. Unlike the <Feedback> section wich is simulating the pipe itself, this section controls the air and its oscillation within the pipe. Thus, this value influences a lot the amplitude interference between the new incoming steam and the reverberating steam inside the pipe.
Note the connection with the <Polarity> button and try different values ...

name: Push
description:
Reverberating Steam Amount
Sets the amount of reverberating steam. Unlike the <Feedback> section wich is simulating the pipe itself, this section controls the air and its oscillation within the pipe.

name: Feedback RT
description:
Reverberation Time
Adjusts the time of the pipe's reverberation, i. e. the amount of damping applied to the feedback's signal before it is mixed again with the new incoming signal. The longer the reverb time, the more the incoming noise steam signal becomes a tone with reckognizable pitch.

name: Feedback Key Track
description:
RT Key tracking
Sets the amount of key tracking applied to the feedback's reverberation time. Turn to the right for longer reverb times at high MIDI pitches.

name: Release Damp
description:
RT Key-Up Damping
Sets the amount of damping applied to the pipe at Key-Up, i. e. at MIDI gate off events.

name: Soft / Hard
description:
Saturation Mode
Controls the way of saturation. Turn to the left for soft saturation, to the right for clipping.

name: Symmetry
description:
Satuartion Symmetry
Controls the szmmetrz of saturation.

name: HP 0
description:
Highpass Cutoff Frequency Low
Sets the cutoff frequencz of an additional highpass filter within the pipe to enhance certain segments of the frequency spectrum of the signal (the formants of the pipe)
Those formants are not modified by the tone's pitch, but by its pressure. By using the MIDI modulation wheel, this pressure can be controlled: At low modulation wheel values this knob is used to determine the formant's frequency, at high mod. wheel values the knob at the right adjusts the formant.
Refer also to the <MW> knobs in the <Del Tune> and <Allpass Tune> sections for further influence possibilities of the MIDI modulation wheel.

name: HP 1
description:
Highpass Cutoff Frequency High

Refer also to the <MW> knobs in the <Del Tune> and <Allpass Tune> sections for further influence possibilities of the MIDI modulation wheel.

name: HP Key Track
description:
Highpass Cutoff Key Tracking
Controls the amount of key tracking applied to the highpss filter's cutoff frequency. Turn to the right for higher cutoff frequencies at high MIDI pitches.

name: LP 0
description:

name: LP Key Track
description:
Lowpass Cutoff Key Tracking
Controls the amount of key tracking applied to the lowpass filter's cutoff frequency. Turn to the right for higher cutoff frequencies at high MIDI pitches.

name: Gain
description:
Master Gain
Sets the master amplification amount in dB. Use the display below to adjust the instrument's level correctly.
